content.rationale:
The remove verb: with no id (ouyrkmlr) it refuses; an argument the form does not name — a flag, or a second id — refuses, named (RM1); an id that maps to neither a valid node nor the root refuses, naming it (D21, tsspuwzo, xtmprysl) — the read is what decides — and removing nothing (qyynqqpx); an id that names no change — the root, the one id that resolves yet owns none, every other such id being D21's — refuses, naming it (RM4); otherwise it abandons the named node's change only when nothing depends on it (D14, stnqmzuw; D7, myprwuxt) — a dependant refuses the invocation, each named (wnxsoknq, zvtktmpz), an unreadable node refuses it, named (RM3), and a gate that evaluates the named node among others refuses it, named (RM2), while the node's own gates are abandoned with it (D7) — the happy path being zrvnlzvw's, bracketed through M-markers-capture (okkvnnvm) — the lifecycle table's removal case (S5-lifecycle, vwlrqoxk) — with changes abandoned through M-jj-abandon (urtkpxwv), S3-abandon's (xllzxxvo) mechanism, the node set scanned through M-node-set (nykqvuqr), and a successful removal writing nothing (O7-remove, loxpnryv). It resolves the id through M-node-resolve (wynwwtur, hence M-node-load), names the file through M-store-path (vkztyrzm), reads through M-store-read across the runner (M-jj), builds its refusals through M-refusal (popowxnw), takes the injected context (M-context zttrwlts, M-context-injection ryuswoxz), and returns its lines for the envelope to write (M-output-return, utrzvyyt) under M-route's handler shape (ynvwvzrm), carrying its own --help text (xlvoxmyl/rwlywqrk, per oqnsuzqu) — answered before the store is taken, so a root-less context still answers it (H1, qtqnuqxo), as do the form's refusals. I1-serde (orrvsxqq) fixes the JSON layer the module is written against — serde and serde_json, the crate's own `Value` and the derive. It hands the store to the capture bracket through the context's fallible accessor, after the surface is answered (S3-root-required). The read's refusal site (S2-read-refusal-site, vollyzvn) is this invocation's: an unreadable node refuses before anything is abandoned, naming it. A removal answers its target even when an abandon refuses partway (S5-record-named, wotmvzyt): the abandons that landed are the window's entries, so the marker is what undo reverts.

This refine adds the draft guard (tzlumxvt, mvxkmrqv) to that same refusal surface, before the capture bracket. `refuse_drafts` scans the work-state registry `.deccy/work/` through `draft_registry::scan` (rroqqrzq, twpvqstu), which reads every document there and refuses rather than silently skips one it cannot read; for each record whose `state` is `open` (vkkwusty) and whose `node` is the id the caller named it collects the record's handle (owyntkvw), and if any are collected the invocation refuses with `a node with open drafts`, every such handle as evidence, and otherwise the guard returns and the removal goes on. A `landed` record is read and passed over, so retention does not withdraw the abandonment from a node that has ever been drafted (vkkwusty); an open record naming another node does not block, because the record's target is one comparison per record and not a key (owyntkvw); and a document the registry's read refuses makes the scan return `Err`, which becomes a refusal carrying the registry's message — the path it refused — so a malformed record refuses the removal instead of slipping past the scan (ntypuupx, rroqqrzq). The guard is asked after `refuse_dependants` and before `markers_capture::capture`, so a node that is both depended on and drafted is still refused naming its dependants first, exactly as D14 has it (stnqmzuw, tzlumxvt), and it only reads: it writes no registry document, moves no operation, and leaves the node set, the changes and the registry byte-identical (tzlumxvt).
